meta.case_name: Why Are Manholes Round / Soft Drink Cans Cylindrical – Creativity

prompt.context: This is a game show / creativity case. There are two standalone brain-teaser questions. The interviewer will ask each question in turn and expect you to brainstorm as many creative, logically grounded answers as possible.
prompt.question:
Question 1: Why are soft drink beverage cans cylindrical?

Question 2: Tell me all ways, practical or not, which you could use to determine whether a light goes off in the refrigerator when you close the door.

framework: Approach each question by considering multiple dimensions: ergonomics/user experience, physics/engineering, manufacturing/cost, logistics/supply chain, and safety.
For the refrigerator light question, think across direct observation methods, indirect/proxy measurement, third-party/manufacturer inquiry, and philosophical/tongue-in-cheek responses.

questions.prompt: Why are soft drink beverage cans cylindrical?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover ergonomics, geometry (volume-to-surface-area ratio), structural integrity under internal pressure, manufacturability, and logistics. A sphere would score on geometry but fail on practicality.

questions.prompt: Tell me all ways, practical or not, which you could use to determine whether a light goes off in the refrigerator when you close the door?
questions.guidance: Strong answers span direct mechanical testing (pressing the door button), physical/sensor-based methods (thermometer, light-sensitive material, electrical meter), statistical/production-line testing, invasive methods (drilling a hole), third-party inquiry, and creative/philosophical responses.

brainstorming.prompt: Why are soft drink beverage cans cylindrical?

categories.name: Ergonomics / User Experience
ideas: Consumers won't cut their hands on sharp edges
Shape is more comfortable and ergonomical to hold

categories.name: Geometry / Material Efficiency
ideas: Maximizes the ratio of volume to surface area short of using a sphere
Delivers more liquid per ounce of aluminum, i.e., more per dollar
A sphere would have the best ratio but is impractical (cannot stand upright, rolls uncontrollably, wastes space in packaging)

categories.name: Structural Integrity
ideas: Circular structures distribute internal pressure evenly
Containers with corners could develop fractures due to high stress concentrations at edges

categories.name: Manufacturing
ideas: Requires the fewest machining, joining, and finishing steps
Least expensive container shape to manufacture

categories.name: Logistics / Assembly
ideas: Rolls predictably and in a controlled manner on assembly lines and in vending machines
Stacks efficiently; spheres would require more air space between units in boxes, vending machines, and trucks, increasing shipping and packaging costs

brainstorming.prompt: Tell me all ways, practical or not, to determine whether the refrigerator light goes off when the door is closed.

categories.name: Direct Mechanical Test
ideas: With the door open, press the button/switch that activates the light to see it turn off

categories.name: Invasive Physical Method
ideas: Drill a hole in the door so you can see inside when the door is closed

categories.name: Indirect Sensor / Proxy Measurement
ideas: Place a sensitive thermometer (pre-chilled to refrigerator temperature) near the bulb and close the door; if temperature rises the light was on
Place light-sensitive material (photographic film, etc.) inside to see if it is activated
Hook up a highly sensitive electrical measuring device to the power source to see if energy consumption drops when the door closes
Hook wires to the socket and measure current when the door is closed

categories.name: Statistical / Production-Line Testing
ideas: Find the mean time to failure for the bulb, close the door, and open it after the expiration period to see if the light burned out
Go to the manufacturer's production line and perform a statistically valid test (appropriate sample size) using the door-button method

categories.name: Third-Party Inquiry
ideas: Pick up the phone, call the manufacturer, and ask whether the light goes off when the door is closed

categories.name: Philosophical / Creative
ideas: 'If no one is in there to see the light go off, does it matter?'

recommendation: Both questions reward structured, multi-dimensional thinking over a single clever answer.
The best responses cover practical, engineering, cost, safety, and creative dimensions without being prompted.
